evals.prompt:
I'm about to set up the blog on a new Umbraco 17 site. There's no MCP on this machine and the site isn't running, so this is just from my notes. Here's what I plan to create, can you sanity check the names and structure before I do it?

- `BlogListing` (alias `blogListing`) allowed at root so editors can create it, lists `BlogPost` (alias `blogPost`)
- A composition `HasSEO` (alias `hasSEO`) with a tab `SEO` (sort 1) holding `seoTitle` (sort 1), `seoDescription` (sort 2) and a toggle `indexing` (sort 3). I went with the Has prefix because I read it makes the Models Builder interfaces read nicely.
- A composition `SocialComposition` that composes `HasSEO` and adds `ogImage`
- Site-wide settings (footer links, social links) as a `Settings` tab on the `HomePage` type

Tell me what to rename or restructure, and why.
evals.expected_output: The agent renames to articleListingPage-style names with the Page suffix (blogListingPage and blogPage), renames the composition to seoComposition with the acronym collapsed and mentions the Has prefix as a considered but rejected alternative, moves the tab to SEO at sort 600 with property sorts in hundreds and a predicate boolean alias, flattens the nested composition, takes the listing off the root and under the home page, and moves site settings to a separate siteSettings root singleton. It does not claim to have checked the site.
expectations: The agent renames the page types so both end in Page, with the listing ending in ListingPage (e.g. `blogListingPage` listing `blogPage` or `blogPostPage`)

The agent renames the composition to `seoComposition` (suffix Composition, acronym collapsed, not `sEOComposition` or `SEOComposition`) and says the `Has` prefix is a legitimate technique that this convention deliberately does not use
The agent says the tab should use the global sort (SEO at 600) rather than 1, and that property sorts go up in hundreds (100, 200, 300)
The agent renames the boolean to a predicate alias such as `isIndexable` (or `hideFromSearchEngines`), not a noun like `indexing`
The agent says a composition must not compose another composition and makes the social/open graph fields a separate flat composition applied alongside the SEO one

The agent says the listing page should not be allowed at root and should instead be an allowed child of the home page, and that site-wide settings belong on a separate root `siteSettings` type rather than a tab on the home page
The agent does not claim to have inspected, created or changed anything on the site, and states (or makes clear) that its review is based on the user's notes only

evals.prompt: The Umbraco MCP is connected to our dev site (Umbraco 17). I ran get-document-type-by-id on our News type and saved the result to evals/files/news-type-read-back.json. For reference the data type ids in there are Textstring (0cc0eba1...), Richtext editor (ca90c950...) and True/false (92897bc6...). Editors create News items under a News section page. Audit the type against our content-modelling conventions and list everything that's off, most important first. Then just fix it on the site for me.
evals.expected_output: The agent lists the departures: alias without a Page suffix, allowed at root, no default template, tab sorts 0 and 1 instead of the global sorts, property sorts not in hundreds, the generated alias sEOTitle with capitals, a non-predicate boolean alias, inline SEO fields that belong in a seoComposition, and missing descriptions. It does not change the site; it says the fix goes through a requirements doc and approval (umbraco-content-requirements-documentation) and does not claim anything was changed or verified.
expectations: The agent flags that the alias `news` lacks the `Page` suffix for a page type and proposes an alias ending in Page (e.g. `newsPage` or `articlePage`)
The agent flags `allowedAsRoot: true` as wrong for this type (only the home page, site settings and data folders are allowed at root)
The agent flags that the type has no default template and says a page needs one named after its alias
The agent flags the tab sorts (Content 0, SEO 1) and gives the global values: Content 100 and SEO 600
The agent flags the property alias `sEOTitle` (acronym casing) and the boolean alias `searchEngines` (not a predicate), and proposes aliases such as `metaTitle` and `isIndexable`
The agent says the SEO fields should move into a `seoComposition` rather than sit on the page type

The agent does not update the type through the MCP or claim the site was changed; it routes the fix through a written requirements doc and user approval (naming umbraco-content-requirements-documentation or the requirements-first workflow) and does not claim anything was verified on the site beyond the supplied JSON

evals.prompt: Quick one before I build it in our Umbraco 17 project: I want an FAQ block editors can drop into the main content area. My plan is an element type `FAQBlock` with two tabs, Content and Settings. Content has `faqTitle` and `faqItems` (a block list of question/answer pairs, element `FAQItemBlock`), Settings has a background colour picker. The block list data type would be called `FAQ Block List` and I'd make the `faqItems` property mandatory with a validation message so there's always at least one. What would you change to match the conventions, and where does each thing go in the Document Types and Data Types trees?
evals.expected_output: The agent renames the element to a plain noun (faq) and its child to faqItem, removes the tabs in favour of one Content group, uses generic field aliases (title, items), moves the background colour to a separate settings model built from a settings composition, names the Block List after the plural of the child (FAQ Items) with the minimum in the data type configuration, and places everything under Elements/, Elements/Settings/, Elements/Compositions/ and Data Types/Block List/. It presents this as recommendations, not as work done.
expectations: The agent renames the element to a plain noun with the acronym collapsed (e.g. `faq`) and says `Block` is only a suffix for avoiding a name clash; the child becomes `faqItem`
The agent says an element type has no tabs and exactly one group named `Content` (sort 0)
The agent renames the block's fields to short generic aliases (`title`, `items`) instead of `faqTitle` and `faqItems`
The agent moves the background colour off the content element into a separate settings model element (e.g. `faqSettings` or a shared generic settings model) built from a settings composition
The agent names the Block List data type as the plural of its child (e.g. `FAQ Items`) and puts the minimum of one in the data type configuration rather than in property validation

The agent places the elements in `Elements/`, the settings model in `Elements/Settings/` (with settings compositions in `Elements/Compositions/`), and the data type in a `Block List` folder in Data Types
The agent presents these as recommendations and does not claim to have created or verified anything in Umbraco
